samples.summary: The assoc-1 selection-mapping block is copy-pasted from `toggleQuote` rather than shared. `commands.ts:301-313` and `list-commands.ts:208-219` now contain the same three-line idiom plus the same explanatory comment (the new comment even says "as `toggleQuote` does"). A tiny shared helper (e.g. `dispatchLinePrefixChanges(view, changes, userEvent)`) in `commands.ts` would keep the two marker-rewriting commands from drifting — note they already differ: `toggleQuote` sets `scrollIntoView: true`, `replacePrefixes` does not, so a bullet toggle at the bottom of a long note behaves differently from a quote toggle. Repo convention favours reuse, but this is small enough to be taste rather than a fit violation.

`docs/design/notes/notes.md` (the canonical notes design doc, "List controls and interactive checkboxes — shipped (issue #754)") still states only "a delegated click anywhere on the item flips that line. The preview never updates its own DOM: the source change re-renders it". The delta adds two load-bearing invariants that the prose no longer describes: (a) a click landing on the real `<input>` is cancelled (`e.preventDefault()`) *before* every bail-out, because a refusal changes no document and therefore triggers no re-render; and (b) `summary` joins `a, button` as a control that owns its own click, coupling the task-click handler to the foldout feature documented separately in the same file. These are behavioural contracts a future editor of this handler must preserve; a sentence in the existing #754 section (not a new doc) would record them. Not an architecture/data-model change, so this does not itself trip the design-doc requirement in CONTRIBUTING.md.

Scope/layering nit: the task-click handler now hard-codes `summary` in its "controls that own their own click" selector, which makes `preview.ts` carry knowledge of the disclosure feature implemented in `details-plugin.ts`. The plugin emits a fixed class (`note-summary`), so the coupling is at least stable, but the general pattern here is a growing untyped selector string (`'a, button, summary'`) that every future interactive element rendered by the preview must remember to be added to (e.g. `input` of other kinds, `select`, `details`). A named constant next to `TASK_ITEM_CLASS`/`TASK_CHECKBOX_SELECTOR`, or a check for interactive elements, would keep the invariant discoverable from the plugin side.
